About Ferro-Alloy Resources Limited:

The Company's operations are all located at the Balasausqandiq deposit in Kyzylordinskoye Oblast in the South of Kazakhstan.

Balasausqandiq is a very large deposit, with vanadium as the principal product together with the CBS and several by-products. Owing to the nature of the ore, the capital and operating costs are very much lower than for other vanadium projects.

The most recent mineral resource estimate for ore-body one (of seven) provided an Indicated Mineral Resource of 32.9 million tonnes at a mean grade of 0.62% vanadium pentoxide ("V2O5") equating to 203,364 contained tonnes of V2O5. In the system of reserve estimation used in Kazakhstan the reserves are estimated to be over 70 million tonnes in ore-bodies 1 to 5, but this does not include the full depth of ore-bodies 2 to 5, or the remaining ore-bodies which remain substantially unexplored.

The grade of carbon in the deposit is over 8%. The carbon flows through to the tailings from where it is concentrated, in a simple low-cost operation, into a 40% carbon product, the CBS, that can be used in place of carbon black as a reinforcing filler in the making of rubber.

The Project will be developed in two phases, Phase 1 and Phase 2, with Phase 1 treating 1.65 million tonnes per year.

The results of the feasibility study, carried out principally by SRK and Tetra Tech, were announced in October 2025, showing a project net present value ("NPV") of US$748m and internal rate of return ("IRR") of 22%.  Since then, a preliminary re-estimation of the capital costs by Chinese engineers China National Chemical Engineering Sixth Construction Co., Ltd has been received, which would have the effect of increasing NPV to US$932m and IRR to 31%.

There is an existing concentrate processing operation at the site of the Balasausqandiq deposit. The production facilities were originally created from a 15,000 tonnes per year pilot plant, which was then expanded and adapted to recover vanadium, molybdenum and nickel from purchased concentrates.  Alongside this operation, there is a well-equipped laboratory and highly skilled technical team, who have already developed the technology that is being built into the feasibility study and is further developing and optimising processes needed for future vanadium and carbon operations. The plant will operate only when profitable concentrates are available and, when not operating as a production facility, will operate on an expanded basis as an R&D centre.

data.title: PayPal Turns to Amex Exec to Take Reins at Venmo — Market Talk
data.description: PayPal is bringing in a new leader for Venmo, its popular payments app that generates meager profits, as part of a broader executive reshuffling. Kartik Mani, who currently serves as president of global network and partner services at American Express, is joining PayPal as president and head of consumer financial services and Venmo. Turning Venmo into a one-stop money-management app, with tools for consumers to keep budgets and invest, is central to plans by PayPal's CEO, Enrique Lores, to run the company as a stand-alone business after a proposed buyout from Stripe and Advent International valued at more than $50 billion stalled. (colin.kellaher@wsj.com)

data.title: Bank of Canada Expected to Raise Rates Once More Even as Consumer Spending Softens — Market Talk
data.description: Consumer spending in Canada is likely to slow in the near term amid softness in the labor market and the squeeze on household incomes from elevated fuel prices and modestly tighter financial conditions, Oxford Economics' Michael Davenport says. The economist notes a weak flash estimate for October retail sales adds to a litany of softer-than-expected data releases since the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in late October. Still, he expects a federal grocery and essentials supplement will give a one-time boost to spending in early 2027. And Davenport continues to expect the central bank will lift its overnight rate a further quarter percentage point in December before moving to the sidelines for an extended pause. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

data.title: A hard landing could be triggered by aggressive rate hikes – BofA
data.description:
Bank of America analysts are warning that the Federal Reserve's aggressive rate tightening cycle risks triggering a hard landing for the economy, with GDP and earnings-per-share growth forecasts likely facing downward revisions.

In a soft-landing scenario, the S&P 500 (SP500) below 7,000 is an attractive buying opportunity, with market breadth improving by spring. If so, investors can position for a shift from rate hikes to cuts by moving into cyclical assets like crypto, chips, copper, consumer stocks, and real estate.

However, BofA analysts believe the likelihood of a hard landing remains underappreciated—they expect GDP and earnings-per-share forecasts to be revised downward and warned that the current AI-driven capital expenditure and wealth-driven “boom loop” could flip into a “doom loop” that forces investors to reduce stock allocations.

For now, with uncertainty elevated, investors are retreating to what they already own and clustering in low-volatility, defensive value positions as they wait to see which scenario unfolds.

BofA drew striking parallels to the 2000 tech bubble, noting that markets were trading in “bubble” territory back in May but are now trading "post-bubble."

During the 2000 bubble's aftermath, staples , utilities , and financials were the biggest outperformers with returns between 45% and 60%, while tech and telecoms were the largest underperformers with returns around -50% and -40%.

The analysts warn that "Fed hikes led to recession and proper bear markets in 2001," and with voters demanding “affordability” through midterm elections, the March 18th or April 28th FOMC meetings represent the earliest points when investors can discount the tightening cycle ending.

The research identified two key economic drivers now under pressure: U.S. household equity wealth, which is down approximately $5T quarter-to-date though still up roughly $8T in 2026, and AI capital expenditure from hyperscalers forecasting $1.3T in spending despite negative free cash flow.

BofA noted that "voters, bond markets, asset allocators are all saying 'slow AI data center buildout,'" which threatens the growth narrative supporting current market valuations.

For recession signals, BofA analysts pointed to unemployment claims and credit spreads as "always best recession tells."

Specifically, claims exceeding 250,000 and investment-grade spreads surpassing 100 basis points would signal the “boom loop” has become a "doom loop," forcing asset allocators to cut stocks and increase allocations to bonds, China, the U.S. dollar, and assets negatively correlated with AI such as real estate—a strategy the analysts describe as "long condos, short chips."

data.title: Klarna partners with Adyen on agentic AI checkout
data.description:
Klarna and Adyen said on Friday shoppers can now pay with Klarna when an AI agent checks out for them through Adyen's agentic suite. It's the first payment option beyond cards available in Adyen Agentic.

Up until now, most AI shopping agents complete purchases with a stored credit or debit card, which precludes flexible payment options that many shoppers choose at regular checkout.

Adyen Agentic and merchants that already offer Klarna through Adyen can switch it on with no new integration work, the companies said.

With Klarna as a payment method within Adyen Agentic, the agent shows shoppers the same Klarna options the merchant already offers, such as paying in full, in interest-free installments, or with financing. Shoppers review and confirm every purchase before it is completed.

Klarna stock slipped 2.3% in morning trading as PayPo, a Polish rival, prepares for a potential initial public offering in Warsaw. Adyeb rose 0.6% in U.S. trading.

data.title: Nvidia's stock heads for a stretch of weekly losses unseen since 2008
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

One fund manager says the continued uncertainty makes Nvidia 'vulnerable' to more selling, even as the company has erased $811 billion in market value in the past seven days

Nvidia's stock is down for the seventh week in a row, a stretch of consecutive losses not seen in nearly two decades.

A cascade of factors has left the stock reeling, most notably Jensen Huang's resignation and the Nvidia (NVDA) board's investigation into whether he compromised national security or revealed corporate secrets. But the stock had been under pressure even before that, with investors questioning the sustainability of artificial-intelligence demand.

Nvidia shares haven't fallen for seven weeks in a row since July 2008, when it had to issue a profit warning and was working to address defects in some of its chips.

Shares of Nvidia were trading 5% lower on Friday. They've lost 13.6% so far this week and they're down 41.2% from their peak close achieved in early October.

Nvidia's stock is down for seven days in a row, over which it has shed $811 billion in market cap. That's roughly the size of JPMorgan Chase, which has a $847 billion market cap, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The stock's "weakness despite strong earnings shows how much it will take to restore confidence." David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, told MarketWatch.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported blockbuster earnings results and raised its revenue outlook for next year, but that wasn't enough to stem the bleeding.

Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg told MarketWatch that fund managers who previously held Nvidia because it was a "safety stock" are now "rotating out" amid the turmoil.

So what comes next?

Goldberg expects things to stabilize next week. "I don't think it keeps falling," he said, though admittedly "there is no one in a hurry to buy it until we know who the next CEO is."

But Miller thinks Nvidia's stock is "vulnerable" to more selling. The length of the losing streak alone "tells us very little about where the bottom is," he told MarketWatch.

"A sharp rebound is certainly possible, but I would want greater clarity on permanent leadership and the investigations, along with continued execution on customer demand and product deliveries, before becoming confident in a sustained recovery," he added.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down more than 9% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $88.16, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer to its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

-Emily Bary
